title: Dredged Material Containment Area (DMCA) O&M Construction IDC
description: Purpose: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah District, is seeking information from industry to determine the availability and capability of qualified contractors is to provide general construction for the new construction, rehabilitation, replacement, repair, and construction-related maintenance of Dredged Material Containment Areas (DMCAs) and associated infrastructure within Savannah and Brunswick Harbors. All work shall be performed in a safe, timely, and cost-effective manner. This notice is issued for the purpose of conducting market research. This is not a Solicitation Announcement, nor is it a Request for Proposal. The Government is contemplating a potential acquisition strategy. The results of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The Government is seeking to identify capable firms, including small businesses, that have recent and relevant experience in performing DMCA-related construction work, such as site preparation, dike construction and repair, weir/structure rehabilitation, erosion control, grading, and general access improvements. Task orders will be executed using the Design-Bid-Build (DBB) delivery method. The Contractor will perform construction in accordance with Government-furnished designs. Requirements: Work under this contract is restricted to the designated DMCAs, bird islands, and directly associated supporting infrastructure located within the Savannah and Brunswick Harbor operational footprints: Savannah Harbor Facilities: Disposal Areas 1N, 2A, 12A, 13A, 13B, 14A, and 14B; Jones/Oysterbed Island (JOI); and associated bird islands. Brunswick Harbor Facilities: Andrews Island DMCA. The Government anticipates awarding a Firm-Fixed Price Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Construction Contract with an expected effective date in late FY27 � early FY28. The anticipated contract period of performance is five (5) years. The contract will provide for the construction, rehabilitation, replacement, repair, and construction-related maintenance of Dredged Material Containment Areas (DMCAs) and associated infrastructure within Savannah and Brunswick Harbors. All work shall be performed in a safe, timely, and cost-effective manner in accordance with the requirements of this contract and individual task orders. The Contractor shall furnish all necessary supervision, labor, materials, equipment, transportation, temporary facilities, construction quality control, and other resources required to complete construction activities under individual task orders in accordance with the applicable contract requirements. Individual task orders will establish specific work limits, requirements, and completion criteria. Task orders will be issued based on the Government�s requirements and may specify performance durations (e.g., calendar days). Representative construction and maintenance tasks may include, but are not limited to construction, rehabilitation, repair, and maintenance of designated DMCA infrastructure, including dikes, embankments, roads, access areas, drainage and water-control systems, shoreline protection, marine access features, and associated structural, mechanical, and electrical components. Supporting activities may include earthwork, excavation, material handling, dewatering, vegetation and debris removal, erosion control, site restoration, surveys, utility protection, temporary facilities, waterborne access, testing, and documentation necessary to complete authorized task orders. All work shall comply with applicable environmental, material handling, disposal, seasonal, and access requirements. General building construction and HVAC work are excluded. Interested Firms: If you are interested in this contract and/or your firm has the potential capacity to perform these requirements, please provide the following information by 27 Nov 2026. � Complete the following survey using the link: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/H8muyzF7RS?origin=lprLink

description: Invitation for Bids (IFB) Set-Aside for Small Businesses NAICS Code: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Massachusetts National Guard intends to issue an invitation for bids to award a single firm fixed-price contract for services, non-personal, to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances and supervision necessary for the construction establish a secure, redundant underground utility corridor (480V power and OSP fiber) to two tie-in points. Work includes approx. 800 LF of horizontal directional drilling (HDD) under airfield pavements at min 8FT depth; primary circuit tie-in splicing into 22.9KV base loop in manhole 110 (EMH 110) with IEEE 386 200A elbows; installation of one pad-mounted transformer (22.9KV prim to 480Y/277V sec, 250KVA) on frost-protected concrete pad; backup system with 400A NEMA 3R manual transfer switch and cannon plug receptacle; and NEMA 3R/4X COMM cabinet with fiber patch panels. Also contains airfield pavement restoration, remarking per UFC 3-260-04, PE-stamped load study, and quality level B sue utility scan at 104 FW, Barnes ANGB, Westfield, MA 01085.The contract duration will be 90 calendar days after notice to proceed to include inspection and punch list. This project is set aside 100% for small business. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, with a small business size standard of $45,000,000. The magnitude of construction is between $250,000 AND $500,000.The tentative date for issuing the solicitation is within the next 30 days (on-or-about December 2026). The tentative date for the pre-bid conference is approximately two weeks following solicitation issuance, time and location to be provided in the solicitation. Interested contractors are encouraged to attend and shall follow conference registration and base access requirements shown in the solicitation. A site visit will follow the pre-bid conference. The bid opening date is tentatively planned for approximately 30 days following the issuance of the solicitation. Actual dates and times will be identified in the solicitation. The solicitation and associated information will be available only from the Contract Opportunities page at SAM.gov. Your attention is directed to FAR clause 52.219-14(e)(3) (DEVIATION 2021-O0008), LIMITATIONS ON SUBCONTRACTING, which states: -By submission of an offer and execution of a contract, the Offeror/Contractor agrees in performance of the contract for General construction, it will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractors 85 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded-. description: NSIC�s mission is to strengthen the national security innovation base by addressing the shortfall of private investment from trusted sources in technology startups developing dual-use hardware products and materials - technologies which have both commercial and national security applications. NSIC funding will enable companies to further develop their products, reducing future technical risk and time to market and increasing prospects for private investment. The current Topics of Interest are found at the NSIC website: https://www.nsic.mil/ This announcement is continuously open; Pitch Decks may be submitted and will be evaluated for the general requirements of the Commercial Acceleration Opportunity (CAO) at any time throughout the year. title: DA10--PACT Act - New Task Order: Cockroach DataBase Licenses and Maintenance (VA-26-00079736)
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Information and Technology (OIT), Product Delivery Services (PDS), Data, Artificial Intelligence, and Innovation Services (DAIS) Portfolio has a requirement for brand name Cockroach Database (CRDB) Subscription Licenses and Maintenance, inclusive of software updates, fixes, security alerts, patches, and 24/7 customer support, herein referred to as software support. VA's existing Summit Data Platform (SDP) requires CRDB, a cloud-native database supporting multi-cloud and hybrid deployments across diverse environments. The SDP requires a database solution that ensures high elasticity and consistency to support mission-critical workloads. This solution must adhere to ACID (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) principles, ensuring reliable data transactions across multiple environments. The database must be deployable across various physical nodes and cloud regions, offering flexibility in scaling operations. The solution must also include non-intrusive, near real-time Change Data Capture (CDC) capabilities, enabling seamless data updates to the SDP. The solution must support multi-cloud hybrid deployments, allowing integration across Data Centers, On-Premise, VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC), GovCloud, and Microsoft Azure Government (MAG) environments. Geo-partitioning is required to optimize latency and ensure consistent and responsive performance for VA operations nationwide. The solution must also provide resilience and elastic scaling to handle machines, datacenter, and regional failures, maintaining continuous operation without manual intervention. Together, these capabilities enable VA to accurately capture operational data and deliver near real-time insight and analytics, ensuring decision makers and customer service staff have accurate, current information to better serve Veterans. The Contractor shall provide up to 300 hours of incidental services support within the 12-month licensing period. This support covers technical assistance beyond standard software maintenance, including configuration and troubleshooting. See attached document J&A Cockroach DB Software Licenses and Maintenance

title: Spain – Laboratory reagents – Suministro de reactivos, material de referencia, material fungible y patrones de las marcas ALDRICH, SIGMA, CERILLIAN, ECACC, GENOSYS, NIST, ROCHE, SIGMAALDRICH, USP (US Pharmacopea), EP (European Pharmacopea) y PHE (Public Health of England) o equivalentes para el Centro Nacional de Alimentación y el Laboratorio de Biotoxinas Marinas de la AESAN OA
description: Tanto el Centro Nacional de Alimentación, como Laboratorio Nacional de Referencia, así como el Laboratorio de Biotoxinas Marinas de Vigo, como Laboratorio de Referencia de la Unión Europea, tienen encomendadas funciones que exigen la realización de ensayos analíticos de gran complejidad que precisan el empleo de reactivos, medios de cultivo, material fungible y patrones de una calidad muy elevada debido a la extrema especificidad y sensibilidad que se requieren en las técnicas de análisis aplicables. La relación de los productos objeto del presente suministro tiene como finalidad cubrir tanto las necesidades que tienen asignadas el CNA como Laboratorio Nacional de Referencia y el LBM como Laboratorio de Referencia de la Unión Europea, así como para los distintos estudios programados por la AESAN OA y las distintas alertas alimentarias.

buyer: Rectorado de la Universidad de les Illes Balears
title: Spain – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – Suministro de un equipo de espectrometría de masas de alta resolución acoplado a cromatografía de gases para los Servicios Científico-técnicos de la Universidad de las Illes Balears, financiado con el proyecto EQC2025-009163.
description: Los Servicios Científico-Técnicos (SCT) de la UIB disponen únicamente de un equipo de GC-MS de cuadrupolo adquirido el año 2005, el cual ha presentado problemas de conectividad y de adquisición de cromatogramas durante los últimos meses, llegando a estar largos períodos averiado, con el consiguiente perjuicio de los usuarios y el desarrollo de sus proyectos de investigación. Debido su antigüedad resulta muy complicado conseguir algunas piezas de recambio para su reparación. Además, el analizador del GC ha quedado obsoleto y no permite la ejecución de análisis MS/MS ni métodos de cribado ni métodos no-dirigidos. El objetivo de este contrato es adquirir un analizador de alta resolución (Q/TOF u Orbitrap) acoplado a GC que permita desarrollar tanto métodos de identificación como cuantificación, en análisis dirigidos, de sospechosos y no-dirigidos mediante MS/MS, con mejor sensibilidad que el analizador disponible en la actualidad. Por ello, en estos momentos, los SCT no son capaces de ofrecer un servicio adecuado acorde a las necesidades de sus usuarios, al no disponer de ningún equipamiento funcional de GC-MS para la determinación cualitativa y cuantitativa de compuestos orgánicos volátiles y semivolátiles en muestras de origen ambiental, biológico, alimentario e industrial presentadas en los diferentes estados de agregación de la materia. El objeto del contrato coincide con el equipo financiado por la Agencia Estatal de Investigación en la ayuda EQC2025-009163.

buyer: Junta de Gobierno de la Diputación Provincial de Burgos
title: Spain – Hazard protection and control consultancy services – Contrato de servicios de consultoría y asistencia técnica para la redacción de los "Planes de actuación de ámbito local" y de las "guías de respuesta ante emergencias por incendios forestales" en el marco INFOCAL
description: Es objeto del contrato la Redacción de los "Planes de actuación de Ámbito Local" y las "Guías de respuesta ante emergencia por incendios forestales" de los municipios de la provincia de Burgos que hayan presentado solicitud en la convocatoria de subvenciones promovida por la Diputación Provincial de Burgos para la elaboración de dichos instrumentos de planificación, y que son los que aparecen en el cuadro siguiente. El objetivo reside en facilitar a los municipios el cumplimiento de las obligaciones derivadas de la normativa vigente en materia de protección civil frente al riesgo de incendios forestales y, en particular, de las determinaciones establecidas en el Plan INFOCAL, dotándoles de los instrumentos de planificación y respuesta exigidos para la adecuada gestión de este tipo de emergencias. El contrato se divide en diez (10) lotes independientes, que corresponden a las distintas comarcas de la provincia, al objeto de favorecer la concurrencia y facilitar el acceso a la licitación de pequeñas y medianas empresas especializadas, siendo estos lotes los siguientes: - Lote 1. Arlanza - Lote 6. Merindades - Lote 2. Bureba - Lote 7. Montes de Oca - Lote 3. Burgos - Lote 8. Odra-Pisuerga - Lote 4. Demanda - Lote 9. Páramos - Lote 5. Ebro - Lote 10. Ribera Los trabajos objeto del contrato se desarrollarán conforme a las estipulaciones técnicas previstas en el PPT que resulta de aplicación y conforme a las cláusulas del presente pliego de cláusulas administrativas particulares.

title: Retail Space to Lease - Delano, CA
description: The Los Angeles District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is seeking to lease a minimum of 1,381 net/usable to a maximum of 1,874 gross/rentable square feet (gross square feet to include any common area factor), of existing Class A or B retail space, in Delano, CA, within the defined Delineated area (DA) boundaries below: North -- South -- East � West � The Government�s desire is for a full-service lease of Retail space for an Armed Forces Career Center for a term not to exceed five (5) years with Government termination rights. Offered space must meet Government requirements per the terms of the Government Lease. Interested respondents may include building owners and representatives with the exclusive right to represent building owners. Representatives of building owners must include the exclusivity agreement, representation letter, listing contract or other executed agreement granting the exclusive right to represent the building owner with their response to this advertisement. Adequate mass transit (buses, trains, rail cars) for the public within three walking blocks is highly desired. REQUIRED Spaces MUST offer both a primary and a secondary point of ingress/egress. Lighted, non-exclusive or reserved on-site parking for four 5 marked government owned vehicles must be provided for on 24 hours 7 days a week basis. Additional lighted parking must be available during business hours, weekends and holidays, for approximately 5 employee vehicles and visitors/recruit candidate parking. Must use the Government Lease. The military services shall have the right to use space beyond normal working hours and, if required, on Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays. This includes the use of elevators, lights, toilet facilities, and, if necessary, heating and air conditioning. Armed Forces Recruiting Facilities are only located in defined geographical areas that contain businesses and other establishments that are of a compatible nature. Under no circumstances will be these facilities to be in areas where sexually oriented businesses, bars, nightclubs, liquor stores, smoke shops, marijuana dispensaries etc. or other business that produce injurious odors detectable with the leased spaces. Placement near these establishments can hamper overall production of the office or cause concern for the safety of the personnel stationed there and their visitors. Lessors are required to be registered and active in www.sam.gov prior to the deadline for final offer submission. Proposals are due no later than 5:00 pm (PST) on November 27, 2026. Responses should include: Building name and address As-built floor plan drawing Digital photo of street view of property Area (BOMA rentable square feet & BOMA usable square feet) Rental rate per square foot rentable space to include (CAM, Taxes and insurance) Common area factor(s) for available space, if applicable Following are the factors that will be considered when evaluating bids/offers: 1. Location 2. Ability to meet all construction specifications, security measures and lease requirements 3. Complete initial and final offers must be received by defined deadline 4. Competitive costs in the best interest of the government 5. Qualitative ratings by client for mission Additional Notes: Three (3) construction bids for the build-out are requested. After a bid is accepted, no change orders are authorized, so bids need to be accurate and complete (including all taxes and fees). Special attention should be given to security requirements (video entry control system, closed circuit television system and video recording, dual roller shades on exterior windows, fixed panel shade on exterior entry door and peep hole in secondary exit, perforated window wrap), fragmentation film on exterior windows/glass doors, telecommunication wiring requirements, addition of water fountain, signage, paint, wall graphics, phone jacks, electrical outlets, and spec'd carpet squares. These are items that can add a significant cost and may be overlooked in the bid process; however, all items in the specifications need to be followed, even if code does not require the item (i.e., smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, etc.). Bids shall include any tear down/haul away expenses. The attached floor plan is to be used as a generalized idea and reference tool for proximity of amount of useable space this location will require for build out in both office space and common area space. Submitted floor plans must meet the space requirements as designated on attached example. It is mandatory that janitorial services be included in the lease (lessor responsible for contracting these services). Be sure to review the attached janitorial guidance and ensure the costs of these services are included on the rental proposal works CONTACT Interested parties may contact Almer Capalac at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Los Angeles Branch, Real Estate Office, (213) 431-5290; almer.capalac@usace.army.mil, no later than 5:00 PM MST on November 27, 2026.

title: PEO-FW FANTOM Behavior Integration (A2E) Assessment Event (AE)
description: PEO-FW FANTOM Behavior Integration (A2E) Assessment Event (AE) Submit NLT 27 November 2026 11:59 PM ET U.S. Citizens Only Purpose SOFWERX, in collaboration with USSOCOM Program Executive Office Fixed Wing (PEO-FW), will host an Assessment Event to identify potential vendors to integrate existing or propose new autonomy behaviors into the government?owned Framework of Autonomous Networked Tactical Open Modules (FANTOM) Autonomy Software using the provided FANTOM Core Software Development Kit (SDK). This event aims to accelerate capability insertion for multi?platform, multi?payload uncrewed systems operating within the Adaptive Airborne Enterprise (A2E) ecosystem. Background/Synopsis A2E is an interoperable system-of-systems designed to enable robust Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities through expendable, autonomous Small Unmanned Aircraft System (sUAS) platforms, resilient data paths, and a common control architecture. FANTOM is the complete autonomy software stack deployed across the A2E System-of-Systems. FANTOM Extensions are mature (high TRL) vendor add-ons integrated using the SDK. Insertion of specialized/new modular, SDK-driven autonomy behaviors is required to extend, mature, and rapidly integrate into the FANTOM ecosystem. Objective USSOCOM is soliciting industry solutions to support FANTOM�s scalable autonomy architecture enabling distributed, collaborative behaviors across Group 2-3 A2E Unmanned Systems (UxS) platforms. As operational demands expand, the program requires continual innovation in: Novel autonomy behaviors (e.g., mission objective/adaptation, swarm coordination, sensing, navigation, task allocation, distributed decision-making, targeting, tracking) Behavior maturation and validation Integration pathways and approaches via the FANTOM SDK (e.g., behavior packaging and versioning, simulation-based evaluation, flight integration readiness) This event will help USSOCOM identify technology providers capable of contributing leverageable behaviors and strengthening SDK integration for persistent autonomy evolution. Desired outcomes include: Catalog of proposed new behaviors and behavior extensions Assessment of vendor capabilities to integrate with the SDK Recommendations for vendors suitable for next-phase development Industry feedback to refine SDK documentation, tooling, and pipelines Why You Should Participate USSOCOM seeks to enter into non-FAR or FAR-based agreements with Industry, Academic, and National Lab partners whose solutions are favorably evaluated by PEO-Fixed Wing Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). As such, the follow-on Assessment Event (AE) is considered competitive, and solutions will be evaluated independently of one another primarily for technical merit. This serves dually as notification of the intent to research the feasibility of an agreement under 10 U.S. Code, Section 4022 and/or Section 4022(f), and as notice of pre-solicitation activities IAW FAR 5.101. Event Timeline Phase 1 - 05 October 2026 to 27 November 2026: Submissions to the Assessment Event (AE) Open: Interested respondents who could potentially provide solutions that meet the needs of USSOCOM are encouraged to submit their capability for USSOCOM review. To submit your technology for potential Phase 3 attendance, please review the assessment criteria and follow the submission instructions at the bottom of this webpage. COMPLETED Phase 1a - 20 October 2026 Q&A Telecon: Interested offerors may participate in a virtual Q&A session to better understand the Program Manager's (PM's) specific technology objectives. The telecon will take place on 20 October from 11:00�12:30 PM ET. RSVP at the bottom of this webpage. Phase 2 - 30 November 2026 to 04 December 2026 Downselect: USSOCOM will downselect respondents/submissions it believes have the highest potential to satisfy its technology needs. Favorably evaluated submissions will receive an invitation to attend the AE on/around 07 December 2026. Phase 3 - 15 - 17 December 2026 Assessment Event (AE): During the AE, selected participants will be allotted a one-on-one session with the USSOCOM evaluation panel to pitch, demonstrate, and/or discuss their solutions. The forum will include a Q&A portion, and discussions may continue outside of the event. Solution brief presentation guidelines will be outlined in the event invitation, and solutions will be assessed according to the criteria in the link provided below. If the USSOCOM evaluation panel favorably evaluates a solution brief, negotiations for Phase 4 may immediately begin. This event will be held virtually. Phase 4 - Path Forward: Successfully negotiated awards may fall under any combination of these categories: Business-to-business research and development agreement as a sub-award through the SOFWERX Partnership Intermediary Agreement (PIA) (15 U.S. Code Section 3715) OTA for research or prototype projects (10 U.S. Code Sections 4021, 4022) An award under 10 U. S. Code, Section 4022 may result in the further award of a follow-on production agreement without additional competition based on successful prototype completion. The Government may make this follow-on production award based upon successful prototype criteria, which will be determined for each prototype project. Procurement for experimental purposes (10 U.S. Code Section 4023) Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (15 U.S. Code Section 3710a) Prizes for advanced technology achievements (10 U. S. Code Section 4025) and/or prize competitions (15 U.S. Code 3719) FAR-based procurement contract NOTE: Awardees may need to be compliant with NIST SP 800-171, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) in Non-Federal Systems and Organizations How You Can Participate Government, Industry, Academia, National Labs, and Non-Traditional Attendees Q&A Telecon Transcript: Click Here to Download Review Assessment Criteria: Click Here to Review Download the White Paper Template: Click Here to Download Complete the Submission Form: Click Here to Submit (NLT 27 NOV)

title: United States – Public relations services – Policy Dialogue and Public Diplomacy Facility for the United States
description: The objective of this action is to strengthen transatlantic collaboration to promote EU interests and priorities in important policy areas, demonstrate the EU's global reach, address global challenges and amplify shared values. Public diplomacy and policy support are relevant tools contributing to improved transatlantic relations: maintaining the EU-US partnership requires actively engaging key stakeholders and audiences to fundamentally raise awareness of the EU, amplify our shared values, and promote the importance of the EU-US relationship among them. On the one hand, the action will enhance EU foreign policy objectives through strategic public diplomacy activities in the United States that engage meaningfully with targeted audiences to build trust and mutual understanding. On the other hand, it aims to provide a framework for rapid action as well as enhancing opportunities for engagement when they arise through a Policy Dialogue Support Facility mechanism. The action enables sustained engagement with decision makers, media and opinion shapers, civil society, business and industry leaders, think tanks, academia, youth, and the cultural and creative sectors. By using a combination of policy dialogue support and public diplomacy, the action will enhance the visibility and credibility of the EU in the USA and contribute to closer alignment between EU and U.S. policy positions and approaches, including on major foreign policy, security, economic, digital and global governance challenges. The action will target federal, State and local level stakeholders on key priority areas based on mutual interest and ability to develop cooperation.

title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE MODIFICATION UNDER CONTRACT N0001421D7003
description: This notice is issued pursuant to FAR 5.101 and FAR 6.103-1(c)(2). The Office of Naval Research (ONR) intends to issue a bilateral modification, to the existing indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) Contract N0001421D7003 with The Pennsylvania State University (PSU). The anticipated modification would increase the IDIQ maximum contract value and extend the contract ordering period from 18 June 2027 through 17 June 2030. The anticipated modification would support the continued performance of the existing requirement for operation and management of the Navy Manufacturing Technology Electronics Manufacturing Center (EMC) and performance of EMC technical research and development projects. Subject to the completion of capability statement review and approval of the required justification, ONR anticipates using the authority at 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1(c)(2), Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. ONR currently believes PSU is the only responsible source capable of continuing this requirement without unacceptable disruption because PSU possesses the resident infrastructure, specialized equipment, and personnel capable of fulfilling the Navy�s complex electronics manufacturing technology requirements without detrimental interruption to ongoing naval acquisition programs necessary to perform the requirement. The Government will review all capability statements received within 15 days of posting this notice before making a final determination. This notice is not a request for proposals or quotations and does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award a contract or modification. Interested responsible sources may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to satisfy the requirement. Capability statements shall address, at a minimum, the ability to: Manage and operate a ManTech Center with effective program, financial, personnel, subcontract, risk, and performance management. Provide advanced manufacturing technical leadership in the Center�s designated technology area through qualified subject-matter experts and technical management. Plan and execute R&D projects supporting manufacturing technology development, maturation, demonstration, and validation. Transition technologies to practice within the U.S. industrial base and into Navy and DoW system applications. Engage the industrial base by maintaining relevant relationships with industry, academia, small businesses, and other manufacturing stakeholders. Maintain required infrastructure and expertise, including access to appropriate facilities, equipment, tools, technical data, and qualified personnel. Serve as a repository of technical knowledge by maintaining expertise, lessons learned, industry information, research results, and transition information in the Center�s technology area. Conduct mission-related studies and surveys, including industrial-base assessments, technology surveys, special projects, and technical analyses. Conduct outreach and technology dissemination through workshops, technical exchanges, demonstrations, industry events, and other activities that promote manufacturing technology adoption. Measure and report results, including technology-transition outcomes, industrial-base impact, cost reductions, schedule improvements, risks, and project status. Provide continuity of operations and a realistic transition approach that minimizes disruption to ongoing Center projects, partnerships, and mission support. Perform additional in-scope mission-support tasks assigned by ONR ManTech Division, consistent with the contract�s defined scope, ceiling, and ordering-period limitations. Ability to assume performance within the required schedule; Approach to avoiding disruption to ongoing Navy technology-development and transition activities; Relevant past performance; and Any information demonstrating that the requirement can be performed competitively without substantial duplication of cost or unacceptable delay. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 541715 with the size standard of 1,000 Employees. A draft Statement of Work is attached to this notice. Responses to this notice must demonstrate clear and convincing evidence that competition would be advantageous to the Government, would not be cost or time prohibitive, and would not hinder the mission objective. All responses must be submitted to the Government Point of Contact at the email address shown below. A determination by the Government not to open the requirement to competition based upon the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government will not be responsible for any costs incurred by responding to this notice.

title: Request for Information - Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Equipment Repair and Maintenance Services
description: **SEE ATTACHED** Information Handling Notice: This RFI is issued for market-research purposes only and does not authorize release of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), Protected Health Information (PHI), or other nonpublic Government information. Respondents shall not submit PHI. Respondents should clearly identify proprietary or confidential commercial information included in their responses. Any future solicitation will identify applicable Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), cybersecurity, safeguarding, and information-handling requirements. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Equipment Repair and Maintenance Services RFI Number: HT941027RFI0001 Issuing Activity: Naval Medical Center San Diego Please submit any questions via email by November 27, 2026 Point of Contact: Dania Suazo, Contract Specialist, dania.suazo.civ@health.mil; Keyshana Harris, Contract Specialist, keyshana.a.harris.civ@health.mil NAICS: 811210 � Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance Estimated Period of Performance: One 12-month base period with four 12-month option periods, if exercised. 1. Purpose This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research and planning purposes. The Government is seeking information from capable GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contractors regarding comprehensive repair, maintenance, and lifecycle-support services for a fleet of gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy equipment. This RFI does not constitute a solicitation, request for quotation, commitment by the Government, or authorization to incur costs. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Any future acquisition, if pursued, will be announced separately. 2. Background The requiring activity operates a fleet of GI endoscopy equipment used in clinical settings. The fleet currently consists of approximately 58 devices, including flexible endoscopes, ultrasound endoscopes, colonoscopes, gastroscopes, duodenoscopes, enteroscopes, and endoscope reprocessors. A detailed equipment inventory, including manufacturer, model, and serial number where applicable, will be provided as an attachment to this RFI or any future solicitation. The Government is assessing the commercial marketplace�s ability to provide a comprehensive, firm-fixed-price service solution that supports equipment availability, patient-care continuity, maintenance traceability, and lifecycle management. The current equipment list includes Olympus GI equipment and OER-PRO reprocessors. 3. Draft Scope of Services The Government seeks industry feedback on the availability and commercial terms for the following services. 3.1 Comprehensive Repair and Maintenance The contractor would provide repair and maintenance support for covered equipment, including as applicable: Preventive maintenance consistent with original equipment manufacturer (OEM) recommendations; Inspection, diagnostics, calibration, functional testing, and quality-control verification; Component-level repair and replacement; Repair of insertion tubes, angulation systems, bending rubber, distal tips, imaging components, fiber-optic systems, light guides, connectors, seals, optical components, and mechanical assemblies; Repair support for endoscope reprocessors; Documentation of pre-repair condition, work performed, parts repaired or replaced, post-repair testing, and quality-control results; and Return of equipment in safe functional condition consistent with applicable OEM specifications and regulatory requirements. The Government expects a contractor to have qualified technicians, an established quality-management system, and appropriate diagnostic and test equipment to support the identified equipment types. 3.2 Service Model and Pricing The Government is interested in commercial service models, including: All-inclusive, firm-fixed-price coverage for all covered repair, preventive maintenance, calibration, testing, labor, parts, shipping, and administrative support; A per-device annual pricing structure; A fixed monthly payment structure; A hybrid approach combining comprehensive coverage with separately priced services; and/or Alternative pricing structures that provide predictable costs and transparent exclusions. Respondents should identify all coverage limits, deductibles, exclusions, repair caps, not-to-exceed limits, surcharges, and conditions that could result in additional Government costs. 3.3 Turnaround Time and Service Levels Respondents should address their standard and expedited repair turnaround times, measured from receipt of equipment at the repair facility or initiation of an onsite repair, as applicable. The Government is particularly interested in industry capability to meet the following target ranges: Repair Category Desired Turnaround Time Minor repair 1�3 business days Standard repair 3�5 business days Major repair/overhaul 5�7 business days, subject to parts availability Respondents should also describe: Repair status notifications and tracking capability; Escalation procedures for delayed repairs; Performance metrics used to measure on-time completion; Corrective-action processes for recurring delays or quality issues; and Emergency or urgent repair support procedures. These ranges are based on commercial service levels identified in the available market information and are provided for market-research purposes only. 3.4 Shipping, Transit, and Loaner Equipment Respondents should state whether they can provide: Prepaid shipping containers, labels, and return shipping; Transit insurance or commercially available alternatives; Equipment intake and condition documentation; Loaner or auxiliary equipment during repair periods, subject to availability; Loaner equipment during extended repair, OEM repair, or replacement actions; and A process for coordinating shipping and repair status with the requiring activity. 3.5 OEM Escalation and Non-Repairable Equipment The Government requests information on the contractor�s ability to address equipment that cannot be repaired in-house. Respondents should identify whether they can: Coordinate OEM or OEM-authorized repair; Coordinate required return material authorization processes; Provide repair, refurbishment, or replacement options; Provide cost estimates and approval procedures before performing work outside comprehensive coverage; Provide loaner equipment during extended OEM repairs; and Identify equipment determined to be at end of useful life and provide lifecycle recommendations. 3.6 Warranty and Quality Assurance Respondents should identify: Warranty terms for workmanship and replacement parts; Quality-management certifications or registrations; Testing and inspection procedures before return to the Government; Procedures for rework or repair failure within the warranty period; Service-record retention practices; and Available documentation to support regulatory audits and equipment maintenance records. The Government is particularly interested in whether industry can provide a minimum 120-day warranty on repair workmanship and replacement parts, or identify an alternative commercial warranty standard. 3.7 Reporting and Account Management Respondents should describe available reporting and account-management capabilities, including: Individual repair reports; Asset-level service history; Repair trends and failure analysis; Equipment utilization or lifecycle recommendations, if available; Annual or periodic service summary reports; Online repair-request and repair-tracking portals; and Designated account-management support. 3.8 Training Respondents should indicate whether they offer training related to: Proper equipment handling; Basic troubleshooting; Preventive-maintenance practices; Reprocessing/disinfection awareness; and Other equipment-care topics relevant to minimizing avoidable damage. title: MH-60R Airborne Low Frequency Sonar (ALFS) Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRA) Support and Sustainment
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), MH-60 PMA-299 (AIR � 2.3.4.2), Patuxent River, MD intends to negotiate multiple sole-source orders over a five-period (FY27-FY31) under Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N00019-26-G-1012 with Thales Defense & Security, Inc. (TDSI), 22605 Gateway Center Dr Clarksburg, MD 20871, to support product support, development, sustaining engineering, repairs, spares, and logistical services associated with the AN/AQS-22 Airborne Low Frequency Sonar (ALFS) system for integration into MH-60R, Multi-Mission Helicopter. This notice also publicizes the government�s intent to negotiate and award the first planned task order under this BOA. This initial order will require a Sustaining Engineering evaluation for three (3) separate Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Specialized Test Equipment (STE) benches. The Government intends to negotiate the initial and all subsequent BOA orders with TDSI under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. This notice is published to identify interested responsible sources and obtain information regarding their capability to meet the stated requirement. The Government will consider timely submissions in determining whether a source is capable of meeting the requirement to satisfy FAR Part 10 and DFARS206.103-170. This notice also serves as the pre-solicitation synopsis requirements of FAR Part 5 for the initial task order. Future orders under the BOA will be synopsized individually as they arise. issued 2.0 REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION 2.1 Overarching BOA Scope The anticipated orders issued under BOA N000926G1012 will encompass product support, Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE), development, and sustaining engineering supplies and services required to support the MH-60R Mission System AN/AQS-22 Airborne Low Frequency Sonar (ALFS) Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs). The primary WRAs include: Transducer Assembly (TA) Reeling Machine (RM) Reeling Machine Interface Unit (RMIU) Reeling Machine Control Unit (RMCU) Reel and Cable (R&C) The five-year scope includes NRE, recurring services, material, component repair, and logistical support to sustain and mitigate obsolescence across both active and delivered systems for the U.S. Navy and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) customers. 2.2 First Planned Task Order Scope The initial order to be executed under the BOA requires a Sustaining Engineering evaluation for the three (3) specific GFE STE benches associated with the AN/AQS-22 ALFS program: Reeling Machine Test Bench (RMTB) Transducer Assembly Test Bench (TATB) Reeling Machine Control System Test Bench (RMCSTB) This effort comprises engineering evaluations, hardware/software analysis, and documentation support to establish the test bench baseline configuration and Technical Data Package (TDP) for each bench., 3.0 SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." TDSI is the U.S. based subsidiary of Thales Underwater Systems SAS (TUS), the original designer, developer, and manufacturer of the AN/AQS-22 ALFS System Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs) for the Transducer Assembly (TA), Reeling Machine (RM), Reeling Machine Interface Unit (RMIU), Reeling Machine Control Unit (RMCU) and Reel and Cable (R&C). TUS owns the proprietary data for these WRAs that is required to perform the efforts herein, including the applicable specifications, source code, and drawings. Thus, TDSI has access and rights to the proprietary drawings and data required to perform these efforts efficiently and effectively. title: Kombispreder for vinterdrift
description: Bakgrunn og formål Arendal kommune har behov for å anskaffe en kombispreder for vinterdrift. Sprederen skal monteres på kommunens eksisterende lastebil og benyttes til salting av utvalgte kommunale veier og arealer. Kommunen har gode erfaringer med salting av de aktuelle veistrekningene og ønsker å videreføre dette. Utstyret som hittil har vært benyttet, har imidlertid vært gammelt og hatt ustabil oppetid. Kommunens tidligere tørrsaltspreder har medført et høyt saltforbruk og ikke gitt ønsket effekt. I forrige vintersesong benyttet kommunen en leid spreder som var ute av drift ved flere anledninger som følge av alder og slitasje. Dette har påvirket driftssikkerheten og beredskapen i vinterdriften. Formålet med anskaffelsen er å sikre effektiv, driftssikker og miljømessig forsvarlig bekjempelse av glatt føre. Utstyret skal bidra til presis dosering og bedre utnyttelse av salt, høy driftsregularitet, god beredskap og dokumentasjon av utført spredning. Utstyret skal benyttes av personell ved Kommunalteknikk, avdeling Anlegg og veidrift. Beskrivelse av oppdraget Anskaffelsen gjelder kjøp av én ny kombispreder for montering på kommunens eksisterende lastebil, Scania 500 med registreringsnummer PD64307. Det åpnes også for alternativt tilbud på én konkret brukt kombispreder. Sprederen skal kunne håndtere tørrsalt og befuktet salt. Leverandøren kan tilby enten ny eller brukt kombispreder, men ikke begge deler. Leveransen skal blant annet omfatte: saltspreder iht. kravspesifikasjonen saltløsningstank komplett styringssystem og betjeningsutstyr montering på kommunens kjøretøy idriftsettelse og funksjonstest opplæring av driftspersonell på Solborg Driftsstasjon Sprederen skal leveres komplett montert og driftsklar. Leverandøren er ansvarlig for å innhente nødvendige tekniske opplysninger om kjøretøyet og dokumentere at tilbudt løsning er kompatibel med dette. Nødvendige adaptere og monteringskomponenter skal inngå i leveransen. Leverandøren skal kunne tilby nødvendig service og teknisk support for utstyret. Det skal også være tilgang på reservedeler i minimum ti år. Priser for verkstedarbeid, service ute hos oppdragsgiver, utrykning og eventuelle løpende kostnader skal oppgis i prisskjemaet. Anskaffelsen kan i tillegg omfatte opsjoner på kamera for livevisning av spredebildet ognekstra fjernkontroll/betjeningsenhet for kjøretøy PD76374. Pris for første ekstra garantiår etter utgang av tilbudt garanti inngår i prisevalueringen, men kjøp av garantiforlengelsen er valgfritt for oppdragsgiver. Type avtale Anskaffelsen gjennomføres som et enkeltstående kjøp av én komplett saltspreder med tilhørende leveranser og eventuelle opsjoner. Det er ikke lagt opp til delkontrakter eller adgang til å gi tilbud på deler av leveransen. Det skal inngås kontrakt med én leverandør. Leverandøren skal ha ansvar for at den tilbudte løsningen fungerer på kommunens kjøretøy i samsvar med kravspesifikasjonen. Verdiberegning Anslått verdi for anskaffelsen er NOK 1 100 000 ekskl. mva. Verdi på hovedleveransen er anslått til NOK 800 000 ekskl. mva. Oppgitt verdi er et anslag og innebærer ikke noen forpliktelse for oppdragsgiver til å anskaffe opsjoner eller andre tillegg utover hovedleveransen. Forbehold Alle forbehold leverandøren har til konkurransegrunnlaget skal oppgis under punktet for forbehold i KGV-løsningen. Alternative tilbud Det er tillatt å levere alternativt tilbud på én brukt kombispreder i stedet for en ny kombispreder. Det kreves ikke at leverandøren samtidig leverer tilbud på ny kombispreder. Andre alternative tilbud tillates ikke. Alternative tilbud på brukt kombispreder skal oppfylle samtlige felles må-krav i kravspesifikasjonen. I tillegg gjelder kravene som uttrykkelig gjelder brukt utstyr.

title: Sonnet Software and Maintenance Support
description: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) intends to negotiate, on a sole source basis, under the authority of FAR 13.106-1(b) (1), with Sonnet Software, 126 N. Salina Street, Syracuse, NY 13202, for the Renewal of Sonnet software and Maintenance Support needed by NIST, Gaithersburg, Maryland. The Sole Source determination is based on the need to renew Sonnet Software and Maintenance Support, which is needed by the Research Facility Operations (RFO) at NIST. NIST currently has a license for the Sonnet platform by Sonnet Software and requires software support services to provide software license maintenance, security upgrades, and technical support for NIST Sonnet software packages. Replacing the software license with another product would result in the following: - Require the purchase of new start-up licenses of the competing product at approximately 4-5 times the cost of purchasing this maintenance and support. - Retraining all staff in the use of the replacement product. - Rewriting all the code written in this product in the format/language/syntax of the new product. Failure to renew Sonnet Software and support will prevent NIST from supporting the current version of the product as it becomes available, including IT security patches and updates. Additionally, NIST will not be able to open tickets for vendor support, and critical IT support will fail to function. Sonnet Software is the only known vendor capable of providing software licenses and maintenance support. The North American Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 513210 � Software Publishers. The small business size standard is $47.0 M. No solicitation package will be issued. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations; however, responses received by 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time on November 28, 2026 will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed acquisition based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Interested parties that believe they could satisfy the requirements listed above for NIST may clearly and unambiguously identify their capability to do so in writing on or before the response date for this notice. This notice of intent is not a solicitation. Any questions regarding this notice must be submitted in writing via email to Prateema Carvajal at Prateema.carvajal@nist.gov. All responses to this notice of intent must be submitted so that they are received at Prateema.carvajal@nist.gov no later than the aforementioned due date.

La part à commande est conclue avec un montant minimum et avec un montant maximum déférents sur chaque lot, conformément aux dispositions de l'article R 2162-4-1 du Code de la Commande Publique.

title: Liquid Chromatography System
description: This is the package is for Maintenance of Chameleon Discovery NX laser Base Period: 12/1/2026-11/30/2027 Option Period 1: 12/1/2027-11/30/2028 Option Period 2: 12/1/2028-11/30/2029 Cost: $19,553.00 Statement of Work The Laboratory of Chemical Physics investigates the molecular structures of protein assemblies that have essential roles in biology and medicine. The research depends on the production and purification of proteins that are labeled with stable isotopes (carbon-13 and nitrogen-15) at specific sites. A liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry instrument, located in building 5, room 103, is required for monitoring the completion of chemical reactions involved in protein production and for verifying the purity of the final products. This instrument requires periodic maintenance, calibration and frequent repairs to replace worn-out or failed components. The objective of this requirement is to ensure that the liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry instrument continues to operate according to its specifications, so that research projects that depend on this instrument can continue to make rapid progress The service contract must cover all components of the LC-MS instrument, including an ISQEM Mass Spectrometer, an Ultimate 3000 LPG-3400SD Low Pressure Mixer, an Ultimate 3000 WPS-3000TSL analytical autosampler, an UltiMate 3000 TCC-3000SD Thermostatted Column compartment, an Ultimate 3000 VWD-3400RS variable wavelength detector, and computer that controls the system. � The service contract must include one annual preventive maintenance visit, during which a technician will test and calibrate all components, replace all parts that require periodic replacement, and perform relevant software upgrades. � The service contract must cover labor, travel, and parts costs for repairs, with a 3-business-day response time. � The service contract must include immediate technical support over the phone or internet when users of this instrument encounter problems or have questions. The vendor shall perform annual preventive maintenance once during the period of performance, on a date requested by users of the LC-MS instrument. The vendor shall provide immediate technical support to users when any problems arise, over the phone or the internet. If a problem can not be resolved remotely, the vendor shall send a service engineer or technician with appropriate expertise to repair the LC-MS instrument within three business days of the initial contact. All costs of labor, travel, and parts will be covered by the service contract, with no additional charges. The Project Officer is responsible for: (1) monitoring the Contractor's technical progress, including the surveillance and assessment of performance and recommending to the Contracting Officer changes in requirements; (2) interpreting the statement of work and any other technical performance requirements; (3) performing technical evaluation as required; (4) performing technical inspections and acceptances required by this Purchase Order; and (5) assisting in the resolution of technical problems encountered during performance. The Contracting Officer is the only person with authority to act as agent of the Government under this Purchase Order. Only the Contracting Officer has authority to: (1) direct or negotiate any changes in the statement of work; (2) modify or extend the period of performance; (3) change the delivery schedule; (4) authorize reimbursement to the Contractor any costs incurred during the performance of this Purchase Order; or (5) otherwise change any terms and conditions of this Purchase Order.

description: DISCLAIMER THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO SOLICIT OR AWARD A TASK ORDER AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS A MARKET RESEARCH TOOL BEING USED TO DETERMINE POTENTIAL AND ELIGIBLE BUSINESS FIRMS CAPABLE OF PROVIDING THE SERVICES DESCRIBED HEREIN PRIOR TO DETERMINING THE METHOD OF ACQUISITION AND ISSUANCE OF A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. Controlled by: DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY Controlled by: NAVAIR CUI Category: General Procurement and Acquisition and Source Selection Distribution/Dissemination Control: FEDCON POC: PMA-266 PCO, kristina.m.johnson79.civ@us.navy.mil Sources Sought RFI Synopsis: MQ-9 Fleet Replacement Squadron Instructor (FRSI) Services (VMUT-2) THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. The responses to this sources sought will be utilized to determine if the Government will competitively solicit via the Kits, Recovery, Augmentation, Components and Engines (KRACEn) Mulitple Award Contract (MAC).[ZS1] [CF2] If two or more KRACEn contract holders are determined capable and qualified, the Government will compete this requirement via the KRACEn MAC. The Product Service Code (PSC) for this requirement is J015. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 336411 (Aircraft Manufacturing) with a Size Standard of 1,500 in number of employees. Requirement Statement: Marine Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Training Squadron 2 (VMUT-2) located at Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Cherry Point, North Carolina serves as the Marine Corps MQ-9 Reaper Fleet Replacement Squadron (FRS), whose primary mission is to train USMC UAS Pilots and UAS Sensor Operators. VMUT-2 is responsible for initial pilot and sensor operator qualification and to graduate basically qualified crews for USMC operational MQ-9 squadrons for follow on tactical training. The purpose of this non-personal services task order is to provide three (3) MQ-9 Pilot flight instructors, three (3) MQ-9 Sensor Operator flight instructors and one (1) FRS Training Specialist to augment the small amount of USMC instructors facilitating student throughput at MCAS Cherry Point. Duties will include live flight instruction, simulator instruction, ground academic instruction and Aviation Training Form (ATF), and academic record keeping. Anticipated Period of Performance (PoP): The anticipated period of performance includes one base period of 12 months with two one-year option periods for a total potential performance period of three (3) years. Capability Statement Requested: A capability statement package no more than ten (10) single-sided 8.5 X 11-inch pages, font no smaller than 10 point, should demonstrate the ability to provide the requirement as listed above. All responses shall include Company Name, Company Address, Company Business Size as it relates to NAICS 336411 under the KRACEn MAC award, Cage Code, and Points-of-Contact (POCs) including name, phone number, and email address. Within your capability statement package, please include your responses to the following information: Ground and Flight Operations. State any experience with supporting Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) ground and flight operations, to include Launch and Recovery Element (LRE) and Mission Control Element (MCE) operations. State familiarity with Flight Operations procedures / Ground Operations Procedures (FOP/GOP) IAW DCMA Instruction 8210.1D. Aircrew Training. State any experience with training basic UAS aircrew, including a list of the type/model aircraft and Programs of Instruction (POI�s) taught. Pilot Qualifications. State any experience with the USAF MQ-9 Initial Qualification Training (IQT), USMC MQ-9 Initial Qualification Training (IQT) or industry equivalent MQ-9 qualification course (i.e. General Atomics-ASI, L3-Harris, Albers, etc.) and include number of live flight hours in MQ-9. Sensor Operator Qualifications. State any experience with the USAF MQ-9 Initial Qualification Training (IQT), USMC MQ-9 Initial Qualification Training (IQT) or industry equivalent MQ-9 qualification course (i.e. General Atomics-ASI, L3-Harris, Albers, etc.) and include number of live flight hours in MQ-9. Classified material SHALL NOT be submitted. All proprietary or corporate data received shall be clearly identified and will be protected from release to sources outside the Government. Any resulting contract is anticipated to have a security classification level of Secret at time of contract award for personnel and facilities clearances. Your response to this Sources Sought, including any capabilities statement, must be electronically submitted in either Microsoft Word or searchable Portable Document Format (PDF) via email to the Task Order Contracting Officer, Kristina Johnson at kristina.m.johnson79.civ@us.navy.mil and Task Order Contract Specialist, Zachary Sinclair at zachary.j.sinclair.civ@us.navy.mil at, no later than 14:00 ET on November 28, 2026 and reference �MQ-9 Fleet Replacement Squadron Instructor (FRSI) Services (VMUT-2) Sources Sought�. title: Graphite Furnace Atomic Absorption Spectrometer
description: Sources Sought Notice for Graphite Furnace Atomic Absorption Spectrometer Notice ID: NIST-MML-FY27-SS01 Response Date: 11/28/2026 Product Service Code (PSC): 6640 NAICS Code: 334516 Background The Inorganic Chemical Metrology Group (ICMG) uses at least two measurement methods, each based on orthogonal physical principles, to certify the trace elements in candidate standard reference materials (SRM). These SRMs are intended for method validation and quality assurance in trace-element measurements to assess the nutritional value and contaminant status of agricultural products. A sensitive trace-element detector, a graphite furnace atomic absorption spectrometer (GFAAS) is sought to complement the group's inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometric (ICP-MS) measurement capability and fulfill the two independent method requirements for SRM development. title: Request for Information (RFI) for Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Protection (JPM CBRN P) Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS)
description: This is a request for information (RFI) only for capabilities and experience which show potential for meeting the requirements described below. This is not a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP) or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). It is a market research tool being used to determine the availability and adequacy of potential sources for planning purposes only. Responses to this notice are not considered as offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of responses nor otherwise pay for the preparation of any information presented or the use of any such information. 1. Purpose The Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Protection (JPM CBRN P) is conducting a market survey to identify industry capabilities, experience, and potential approaches for serving as a Product Support Integrator (PSI) and material integration support for the Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS) Reconfiguration and Technology Refresh effort. The Government seeks a commercial partner capable of procuring and coordinating the delivery of commercially available components; receiving, tracking, and consolidating Government-sourced components; applying Item Unique Identification (IUID) markings as required; maintaining materiel accountability and readiness; conducting Preventative Maintenance, Checks and Services (PMCS) and Care of Supply in Storage (COSIS) as necessary, and delivering verified, complete component packages to Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA) for final system integration, build completion, and packaging. This RFI is issued solely for planning and market-research purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, commitment by the Government, or authorization to incur costs. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. 2. Background CP DEPMEDS is a fielded CBRN protection system that supports Army Role 3 field-hospital operations. The program is executing a reconfiguration and technology-refresh effort using fielded, previously qualified, and commercially available components. The revised support concept under consideration would use a commercial PSI to integrate component procurement, Government-furnished or Government-sourced materiel coordination, traceability, IUID marking, and delivery to Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA). PBA would retain responsibility for final assembly/integration of CP DEPMEDS sets, final packaging, associated Government acceptance activities, and delivery of sets to their fielding/final destination. 3. Scope of Information Requested The Government seeks information on industry capability to perform the following functions: A. Commercial Component Procurement Procure commercially available components identified by the Government. Conduct vendor management and order placement of components. Identify long-lead items, supply-chain constraints, discontinuance risks, and proposed alternate sources. Provide proposed substitutes only when specifically authorized by the Government. Manage warranties, vendor documentation, certificates of conformance, and commercial shipping documentation as applicable. B. Government Component Coordination Coordinate receipt, transfer, and consolidation of Government-sourced components from designated Government organizations, depots, supply activities, or other locations. Maintain accountability for Government-provided or Government-directed materiel while in contractor custody. Maintain COSIS to prevent environmental degradation, corrosion, and shelf life expiration of stored equipment and supplies. Reconcile shipping discrepancies, damaged materiel, shortages, overages, and documentation issues. Maintain traceability between each component, its source, and its assigned CP DEPMEDS configuration or set. Note: The contractor would not independently obligate Government funds or direct Government supply activities. The Government would retain authority for requisitions, funding, release, acceptance, and disposition decisions. C. IUID and Asset Identification Apply, validate, and document IUID markings for designated end items and components in accordance with Government-furnished requirements and applicable standards. Verify marking quality, placement, readability, and association with the correct item record. Maintain item-level records linking serial number, part number, National Stock Number, Unique Item Identifier, source, and destination. Provide electronic IUID and asset-accountability data deliverables in a Government-specified format. D. Materiel Receiving, Inspection, and Staging Receive and inspect commercial and Government-sourced components. Verify quantities, part numbers, serial numbers, condition, shelf life, and required documentation. Store and stage components in a manner that preserves condition, supports shelf-life management, and enables rapid consolidation into required delivery packages. Maintain COSIS to prevent environmental degradation, corrosion, and shelf life expiration of stored equipment and supplies. E. Kit Completion and Delivery to PBA Build component-level shipping packages in accordance with Government-approved bills of material, configuration lists, and delivery priorities. Conduct kit-completeness checks before shipment. Package, preserve, mark, and ship components to PBA in accordance with Government-approved shipping instructions. Provide advance-shipment notifications, packing lists, serial-number/IUID records, and discrepancy reports. If required, travel to PBA to help support the delivery and inventory of shipped equipment. F. Program Management and Reporting Maintain an integrated procurement and delivery schedule. Provide recurring status reports addressing procurement status, component availability, shortages, long-lead risks, delivery forecasts, IUID status, kit completion, and shipment status. Identify risks early and recommend mitigation actions, including alternate vendors, phased deliveries, or proposed substitutes. Participate in Government-led integrated product team meetings as required. 4. Desired Capabilities Respondents should describe experience performing comparable work involving: Multi-vendor procurement and materiel integration; Government-furnished property or Government-directed materiel; IUID marking, validation, and data management; Military logistics, asset accountability, and shipping documentation; Kitting, staging, packaging, preservation, and shipment of complex equipment; Supply-chain risk management and long-lead-item mitigation; CBRN, deployable medical, field-hospital, shelter, or comparable expeditionary equipment. (Note: This is desired experience but not required for response.) The Government is particularly interested in respondents able to manage multiple sources of supply and coordinate delivery of components to a Government integration location. 5. Industry Response Instructions Responses should not exceed [15] pages, excluding attachments. Include: Company Information: Name, UEI, CAGE code, business size, socioeconomic status, and points of contact. Relevant Experience: Up to three relevant efforts performed within the past five years. Technical Approach: Notional approach to commercial procurement, Government-component coordination, IUID, accountability, staging, kit verification, and delivery to PBA. Facilities and Workforce: Relevant facilities, quality systems, logistics staff, IUID capability, and geographic support model. Data and Reporting: Proposed methods for inventory visibility, serialized-item traceability, IUID data delivery, and Government status reporting. Risk Management: Principal risks, including vendor lead time, part obsolescence, Government materiel availability, configuration changes, and transportation delays.
